02---areas/k8s/11-production-deployment/.title: 11.7. Cost Optimization
02---areas/k8s/11-production-deployment/.content:
11.7. Cost Optimization

Giảm chi phí K8s mà vẫn đảm bảo performance và reliability


🎯 Mục Tiêu

✅ Hiểu FinOps framework cho Kubernetes
✅ Triển khai Resource right-sizing (VPA, actual usage analysis)
✅ Tối ưu với Spot/Preemptible instances và PDB
✅ Setup Cost monitoring với Kubecost/OpenCost
✅ Implement Dev/test scheduling (scale to zero off-hours)
✅ Áp dụng Multi-tenancy cost allocation
✅ Tối ưu Storage và Network costs


💰 FinOps Framework
FinOps Là Gì?
FinOps = Financial Operations for Cloud
= Collaboration giữa Engineering ↔ Finance ↔ Business

Kubernetes FinOps challenges:
├── Shared clusters → khó allocate cost per team
├── Dynamic scaling → cost unpredictable
├── Over-provisioning → waste (phổ biến nhất!)
├── Under-provisioning → performance issues
└── Lack of visibility → không biết money đi đâu

FinOps Lifecycle
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   FinOps LIFECYCLE                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                         │
│  1. INFORM (Visibility)                                │
│  ├── Allocate costs per team/namespace/app             │
│  ├── Dashboard: Who spends what?                       │
│  ├── Showback/Chargeback reports                       │
│  └── Tools: Kubecost, OpenCost                         │
│                                                         │
│  2. OPTIMIZE (Efficiency)                              │
│  ├── Right-size resources (VPA recommendations)        │
│  ├── Use spot instances                                │
│  ├── Schedule dev/test environments                    │
│  ├── Remove unused resources                           │
│  └── Optimize storage tiers                            │
│                                                         │
│  3. OPERATE (Governance)                               │
│  ├── Set budgets per team                              │
│  ├── Alert on cost anomalies                           │
│  ├── Enforce resource requests/limits                  │
│  ├── Regular cost reviews                              │
│  └── Continuous improvement                            │
│                                                         │
│  → Repeat: INFORM → OPTIMIZE → OPERATE                 │
│                                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


📊 Cost Monitoring
Kubecost (Feature-rich, K8s-specific)
# Install Kubecost
helm repo add kubecost kubecost.github.io/cost-analyzer/
helm install kubecost kubecost/cost-analyzer \
  --namespace kubecost \
  --create-namespace \
  --set kubecostToken="<free-token>"  # Free tier available
 
# Access UI
kubectl port-forward svc/kubecost-cost-analyzer 9090:9090 -n kubecost
# Open: http://localhost:9090
Kubecost cung cấp:
├── Cost per namespace, deployment, pod
├── Idle resource detection (→ wasted spend)
├── Right-sizing recommendations
├── Savings opportunities
├── Cost trends and forecasting
├── Network cost allocation
├── Shared cost allocation
└── Alerts on anomalies

OpenCost (Open source, CNCF)
# Install OpenCost
helm repo add opencost opencost.github.io/opencost-helm-chart
helm install opencost opencost/opencost \
  --namespace opencost \
  --create-namespace
 
# Integrate với Grafana
# Import OpenCost dashboard
Key Cost Metrics
Metrics to track:
├── Total cluster cost (monthly)
├── Cost per namespace (team/project)
├── Cost per deployment
├── Idle cost (requested nhưng không dùng)
├── CPU/Memory efficiency (actual / requested)
├── Cost per request (application-level)
└── Cost trend (month-over-month)

Typical waste:
├── 30-60% of requested CPU unused (idle)
├── 20-40% of requested memory unused
├── 15% of PVs không attached
└── Dev environments run 24/7 (dùng 8 giờ/ngày)


💡 Resource Right-Sizing
Step 1: Analyze Actual Usage
# Check actual resource usage
kubectl top pods -n production --sort-by=cpu
kubectl top pods -n production --sort-by=memory
 
# Compare requests vs actual
kubectl get pods -n production -o custom-columns=\
  NAME:.metadata.name,\
  CPU_REQ:.spec.containers[0].resources.requests.cpu,\
  CPU_LIM:.spec.containers[0].resources.limits.cpu,\
  MEM_REQ:.spec.containers[0].resources.requests.memory,\
  MEM_LIM:.spec.containers[0].resources.limits.memory
Step 2: VPA Recommendations
# VPA trong mode "Off" → chỉ recommend, không tự thay đổi
apiVersion: autoscaling.k8s.io/v1
kind: VerticalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: myapp-vpa
  namespace: production
spec:
  targetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: myapp
  updatePolicy:
    updateMode: "Off"  # Chỉ recommend
  resourcePolicy:
    containerPolicies:
    - containerName: app
      minAllowed:
        cpu: 50m
        memory: 64Mi
      maxAllowed:
        cpu: 2
        memory: 4Gi
      controlledResources: ["cpu", "memory"]
# Xem recommendations
kubectl describe vpa myapp-vpa -n production
# Recommendation:
#   Container Recommendations:
#     Container Name: app
#     Lower Bound:    CPU: 50m,  Memory: 128Mi
#     Target:         CPU: 200m, Memory: 256Mi   ← Nên set
#     Upper Bound:    CPU: 500m, Memory: 512Mi
#     Uncapped Target: CPU: 200m, Memory: 256Mi
Step 3: Apply Right-Sized Values
# Before (over-provisioned)
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 1000m        # Requesting 1 CPU
    memory: 2Gi       # Requesting 2 GiB
  limits:
    cpu: 2000m
    memory: 4Gi
 
# After (right-sized, based on VPA recommendation)
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 200m         # 5x reduction! 💸
    memory: 256Mi     # 8x reduction! 💸
  limits:
    cpu: 500m
    memory: 512Mi
Common Over-Provisioning Patterns
🚨 Pattern 1: "Just to be safe" — requests = limits = high values
   ❌ cpu: 2, memory: 4Gi (nhưng thực tế dùng 100m CPU, 200Mi memory)
   ✅ Dùng VPA recommendations, set requests = actual + 20% buffer

🚨 Pattern 2: Copy-paste từ StackOverflow
   ❌ Mọi service đều 500m CPU, 512Mi memory (one-size-fits-all)
   ✅ Profile từng service riêng

🚨 Pattern 3: Never review after initial setup
   ❌ Set once, forget forever
   ✅ Review monthly, adjust seasonally


🎰 Spot / Preemptible Instances
Cách Hoạt Động
On-Demand instances: Full price, guaranteed availability
Spot instances:      60-91% cheaper, can be terminated with 2-min warning!

Strategy:
├── Stateless workloads → Spot instances ✅
├── Stateful workloads → On-Demand ❌ (don't put databases on spot!)
├── Batch jobs → Spot instances ✅
└── Critical APIs → Mix (on-demand base + spot for burst)

Node Pool Configuration
GKE:
resource "google_container_node_pool" "spot" {
  name    = "spot-pool"
  cluster = google_container_cluster.primary.id
  
  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 0
    max_node_count = 10
  }
  
  node_config {
    machine_type = "n2-standard-8"
    spot         = true
    
    # Taint spot nodes: chỉ workloads có toleration mới schedule
    taint {
      key    = "cloud.google.com/gke-spot"
      value  = "true"
      effect = "NoSchedule"
    }
    
    labels = {
      "pool-type" = "spot"
    }
  }
}
EKS:
apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5
kind: ClusterConfig
metadata:
  name: my-cluster
managedNodeGroups:
- name: spot-workers
  instanceTypes: ["m5.xlarge", "m5a.xlarge", "m5d.xlarge"]  # Multi-type!
  spot: true
  minSize: 0
  maxSize: 10
  labels:
    pool-type: spot
  taints:
  - key: spot
    value: "true"
    effect: NoSchedule
Workload Configuration for Spot
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: batch-processor
spec:
  replicas: 5
  template:
    spec:
      # Tolerate spot nodes
      tolerations:
      - key: "cloud.google.com/gke-spot"
        operator: "Equal"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      
      # Prefer spot nodes
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - weight: 100
            preference:
              matchExpressions:
              - key: pool-type
                operator: In
                values: ["spot"]
      
      # Handle termination gracefully
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      containers:
      - name: processor
        image: batch-processor:v1
        # Application PHẢI handle SIGTERM gracefully!
Pod Disruption Budget (PDB)
Đảm bảo availability khi spot nodes bị terminate:
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: myapp-pdb
  namespace: production
spec:
  # Luôn giữ ít nhất 2 pods running
  minAvailable: 2
  # Hoặc: cho phép tối đa 1 pod unavailable
  # maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp

⏰ Dev/Test Environment Scheduling
Scale to Zero Off-Hours
Vấn đề: Dev/test clusters chạy 24/7 nhưng chỉ dùng 8-10 giờ/ngày → 60% waste!
# CronJob: Scale DOWN lúc 8 PM
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: scale-down-dev
  namespace: kube-system
spec:
  schedule: "0 20 * * 1-5"  # 8 PM Mon-Fri
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: scaler-sa  # Cần RBAC!
          containers:
          - name: scale
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - |
              kubectl scale deployment --all --replicas=0 -n development
              kubectl scale deployment --all --replicas=0 -n staging
              echo "Scaled down dev/staging at $(date)"
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
# CronJob: Scale UP lúc 8 AM
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: scale-up-dev
  namespace: kube-system
spec:
  schedule: "0 8 * * 1-5"  # 8 AM Mon-Fri
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: scaler-sa
          containers:
          - name: scale
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - |
              # Restore to documented replica counts
              kubectl scale deployment frontend --replicas=2 -n development
              kubectl scale deployment backend --replicas=2 -n development
              kubectl scale deployment frontend --replicas=2 -n staging
              kubectl scale deployment backend --replicas=2 -n staging
              echo "Scaled up dev/staging at $(date)"
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
Cluster Autoscaler + Scale to Zero
# Cluster Autoscaler config
autoscaling:
  min_node_count: 0    # Scale to ZERO nodes when no workloads!
  max_node_count: 10
  
# Combined với scale-down CronJob:
# 1. CronJob scales deployments to 0 replicas
# 2. No pods to schedule → Cluster Autoscaler removes idle nodes
# 3. Node count → 0
# 4. Cost → near $0 (chỉ trả control plane)

🏷️ Multi-Tenancy Cost Allocation
Label Strategy
# Mandatory labels cho cost allocation
metadata:
  labels:
    team: backend             # Team owner
    product: checkout         # Product/feature
    environment: production   # Environment
    cost-center: CC-1234      # Finance code
Enforce Labels với Policy Engine
# Kyverno: Require cost labels
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-cost-labels
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-labels
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Deployment
          - StatefulSet
    validate:
      message: "Must include labels: team, product, environment, cost-center"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          labels:
            team: "?*"
            product: "?*"
            environment: "?*"
            cost-center: "?*"
ResourceQuota Per Team
# Team A: 20% cluster capacity
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-a-quota
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "8"
    requests.memory: 16Gi
    limits.cpu: "16"
    limits.memory: 32Gi
    pods: "50"
    persistentvolumeclaims: "10"
---
# Team B: 30% cluster capacity
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-b-quota
  namespace: team-b
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "12"
    requests.memory: 24Gi
    limits.cpu: "24"
    limits.memory: 48Gi
    pods: "80"
    persistentvolumeclaims: "20"
Showback vs Chargeback
Showback: "Here's what your team costs"
├── Informational — no actual billing
├── Encourages awareness
├── Monthly reports
└── Dùng khi: Internal teams, shared budget

Chargeback: "Your team pays for this"
├── Actual billing to team budget
├── Incentivizes optimization
├── Accurate allocation needed
└── Dùng khi: Large organizations, separate P&L


📦 Storage Optimization
Use Appropriate Storage Tiers
# Standard (cheap, slower — HDD)
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: standard
provisioner: kubernetes.io/gce-pd
parameters:
  type: pd-standard
# Cost: ~$0.04/GB/month
 
---
# SSD (expensive, fast)
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-ssd
provisioner: kubernetes.io/gce-pd
parameters:
  type: pd-ssd
# Cost: ~$0.17/GB/month (4x more expensive!)
 
# Rule: Dùng SSD cho databases cần IOPS
#        Dùng Standard cho logs, backups, archives
Cleanup Unused Resources
# Find unbound PVs (Released state)
kubectl get pv --field-selector=status.phase=Released
 
# Find PVCs not used by any Pod
kubectl get pvc --all-namespaces -o json | \
  jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Bound") | 
  "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'
 
# Find unused ConfigMaps
kubectl get configmaps --all-namespaces -o json | \
  jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.ownerReferences == null) | 
  .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' | head -20
 
# Find unused Secrets (không active reference)
# ⚠️ Cẩn thận — verify trước khi xóa!
kubectl get secrets --all-namespaces --field-selector=type=Opaque -o json | \
  jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' | head -20
 
# Delete unused PVs (after verification!)
# kubectl delete pv <pv-name>

📈 Cost Savings Examples
Scenario 1: Resource Right-Sizing
Before: 20 pods × (1 CPU, 2Gi) = 20 CPU, 40Gi requested
Actual usage: 20 pods × (200m CPU, 400Mi) = 4 CPU, 8Gi used
Waste: 80% CPU, 80% Memory!

After right-sizing: 20 pods × (300m CPU, 512Mi) = 6 CPU, 10Gi
Savings: 70% CPU, 75% Memory
Monthly savings: ~$500-1000 (depends on provider)

Scenario 2: Spot Instances
Before: 10 on-demand nodes × $200/month = $2,000/month
After:  3 on-demand + 7 spot nodes = 3×$200 + 7×$60 = $1,020/month
Savings: 49% ($980/month)

Scenario 3: Dev/Test Scheduling
Before: Dev cluster 24/7 = $1,500/month
After:  Dev cluster 10h/day × 5 days/week = $450/month
Savings: 70% ($1,050/month)

Scenario 4: Combined Optimizations
┌─────────────────────────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
│ Optimization            │ Before   │ After    │ Savings  │
├─────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────┤
│ Right-sizing            │ $3,000   │ $1,200   │ $1,800   │
│ Spot instances          │ $2,000   │ $1,000   │ $1,000   │
│ Dev/test scheduling     │ $1,500   │ $450     │ $1,050   │
│ Storage optimization    │ $500     │ $200     │ $300     │
│ Unused resource cleanup │ $300     │ $0       │ $300     │
├─────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────┤
│ TOTAL                   │ $7,300   │ $2,850   │ $4,450   │
│                         │          │          │ (61%)    │
└─────────────────────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘


💡 Cost Optimization Checklist
✅ Quick Wins (Implement Today)
□ Delete unused PVs, ConfigMaps, Secrets
□ Stop dev/test during off-hours
□ Remove :latest tags (unnecessary pulls)
□ Set resource requests based on actual usage
□ Install Kubecost/OpenCost for visibility

✅ Medium-Term (This Month)
□ Implement VPA recommendations
□ Setup spot node pools for non-critical workloads
□ Configure PDB for spot resilience
□ Add cost labels to all resources
□ Setup cost alerts (budget thresholds)

✅ Long-Term (This Quarter)
□ Implement ResourceQuota per team
□ Setup showback/chargeback reporting
□ Optimize storage tiers
□ Review HPA/VPA configurations
□ Regular cost review meetings (monthly)
□ Evaluate Reserved Instances vs On-Demand


🎓 Key Takeaways

FinOps = Inform → Optimize → Operate (continuous cycle)
Right-sizing giảm 40-70% waste — dùng VPA recommendations
Spot instances giảm 60-91% compute cost — dùng cho stateless workloads
Dev/test scheduling giảm 60-70% cost — scale to zero off-hours
Cost allocation bằng labels + ResourceQuota — accountability per team
Monitor costs liên tục — Kubecost/OpenCost dashboards
Storage tiers — standard cho logs/archives, SSD chỉ cho databases
Quick wins → Medium term → Long term: progressive optimization

02---areas/k8s/11-production-deployment/.title: 11.8. Troubleshooting Production Issues
02---areas/k8s/11-production-deployment/.content:
11.8. Troubleshooting Production Issues

Systematic approach để debug và fix production issues


🎯 Mục Tiêu

✅ Systematic debugging workflow
✅ Common production issues và fixes
✅ Essential kubectl commands
✅ Log analysis techniques
✅ Performance troubleshooting


🔍 Debugging Workflow
Systematic Approach
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   1. IDENTIFY THE PROBLEM               │
│   • What is broken?                     │
│   • When did it start?                  │
│   • What changed recently?              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   2. GATHER INFORMATION                 │
│   • Check logs                          │
│   • Check metrics                       │
│   • Check events                        │
│   • Check resource usage                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   3. FORM HYPOTHESIS                    │
│   • What could cause this?              │
│   • Most likely root cause?             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   4. TEST HYPOTHESIS                    │
│   • Verify theory                       │
│   • Check related components            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   5. IMPLEMENT FIX                      │
│   • Apply fix                           │
│   • Monitor results                     │
│   • Verify fix works                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│   6. DOCUMENT & PREVENT                 │
│   • Write post-mortem                   │
│   • Update runbooks                     │
│   • Implement prevention                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘


🚨 Common Production Issues
Issue 1: Pod Stuck in Pending State
Symptoms:
$ kubectl get pods
NAME                 READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
myapp-abc123-xyz     0/1     Pending   0          5m
Debugging Steps:
# 1. Describe pod để xem events
kubectl describe pod myapp-abc123-xyz
 
# Common causes trong events:
# "Insufficient cpu"
# "Insufficient memory"
# "No nodes available"
# "Pod has unbound PersistentVolumeClaims"
Root Causes & Fixes:
A. Insufficient Resources:
# Check node capacity
kubectl top nodes
kubectl describe nodes
 
# Fix: Scale cluster hoặc giảm resource requests
kubectl scale deployment myapp --replicas=2  # Temporary
# Hoặc update resource requests trong Deployment
B. Node Selector/Affinity Issues:
# Check pod spec
kubectl get pod myapp-abc123-xyz -o yaml | grep -A 10 nodeSelector
 
# Fix: Remove hoặc adjust nodeSelector/affinity
kubectl edit deployment myapp
# Xóa hoặc sửa nodeSelector section
C. Unbound PVC:
# Check PVCs
kubectl get pvc
NAME        STATUS    VOLUME   CAPACITY   STORAGECLASS
data-pvc    Pending   -        -          standard
 
# Check storage class
kubectl get storageclass
 
# Fix: Create PV hoặc use dynamic provisioning
kubectl apply -f pv.yaml

Issue 2: CrashLoopBackOff
Symptoms:
$ kubectl get pods
NAME                 READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
myapp-abc123-xyz     0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   5          10m
Debugging:
# 1. Check logs
kubectl logs myapp-abc123-xyz
kubectl logs myapp-abc123-xyz --previous  # Logs from crashed container
 
# 2. Describe pod
kubectl describe pod myapp-abc123-xyz
 
# 3. Check events
kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | grep myapp
Common Root Causes:
A. Application Error:
# Logs show:
# "Error: Cannot connect to database"
# "Fatal: Missing environment variable API_KEY"
 
# Fix: Check ConfigMap/Secret
kubectl get configmap myapp-config -o yaml
kubectl get secret myapp-secrets -o yaml
 
# Verify environment variables trong pod
kubectl exec myapp-abc123-xyz -- env
B. Liveness Probe Failing:
# Check probe configuration
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 10  # Too short?
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 3
 
# Fix: Increase initialDelaySeconds
# Application có thể cần thời gian khởi động
livenessProbe:
  initialDelaySeconds: 60  # Increase
C. Out of Memory (OOMKilled):
# Describe pod sẽ show:
# Last State: Terminated
#   Reason: OOMKilled
#   Exit Code: 137
 
# Check memory usage
kubectl top pod myapp-abc123-xyz
 
# Fix: Increase memory limits
resources:
  limits:
    memory: 1Gi  # Increase từ 512Mi
  requests:
    memory: 512Mi

Issue 3: Service Không Accessible
Symptoms:
# Curl to service fails
$ kubectl run test --rm -it --image=busybox -- wget -O- http://myapp-service
wget: can't connect to remote host: Connection refused
Debugging:
# 1. Check service
kubectl get svc myapp-service
kubectl describe svc myapp-service
 
# 2. Check endpoints
kubectl get endpoints myapp-service
 
# No endpoints? → Service selector không match Pods
Root Causes:
A. Service Selector Mismatch:
# Check service selector
kubectl get svc myapp-service -o yaml | grep -A 5 selector
 
# Check pod labels
kubectl get pods --show-labels
 
# Fix: Update service selector to match pod labels
kubectl edit svc myapp-service
B. Pods Not Ready:
# Check pod status
kubectl get pods -l app=myapp
 
# Pods Running but NOT Ready? Check readiness probe
kubectl describe pod myapp-abc123-xyz | grep -A 10 Readiness
 
# Fix readiness probe issues
C. Network Policy Blocking:
# Check network policies
kubectl get networkpolicies
 
# Describe policy
kubectl describe networkpolicy myapp-netpol
 
# Fix: Adjust network policy to allow traffic

Issue 4: High CPU/Memory Usage
Symptoms:
$ kubectl top pods
NAME                 CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
myapp-abc123-xyz     980m         1900Mi
 
# Pod using 98% của limit!
Debugging:
# 1. Check resource limits
kubectl describe pod myapp-abc123-xyz | grep -A 10 Limits
 
# 2. Profile application
kubectl exec myapp-abc123-xyz -- top
kubectl exec myapp-abc123-xyz -- ps aux
 
# 3. Check for memory leaks
# Monitor memory over time
watch kubectl top pod myapp-abc123-xyz
Fixes:
A. Increase Limits (short-term):
resources:
  limits:
    cpu: 2000m      # Increase
    memory: 3Gi     # Increase
  requests:
    cpu: 1000m
    memory: 1Gi
B. Optimize Application (long-term):
• Profile code (CPU/memory profiling)
• Fix memory leaks
• Optimize database queries
• Add caching
• Use connection pooling

C. Scale Horizontally:
# Add more replicas thay vì increase limits
kubectl scale deployment myapp --replicas=5

Issue 5: ImagePullBackOff
Symptoms:
$ kubectl get pods
NAME                 READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
myapp-abc123-xyz     0/1     ImagePullBackOff   0          2m
Debugging:
# Describe pod
kubectl describe pod myapp-abc123-xyz
 
# Events sẽ show:
# Failed to pull image "gcr.io/project/myapp:v1.0"
# Error: unauthorized / not found / timeout
Root Causes:
A. Image Doesn’t Exist:
# Check image tag
kubectl get deployment myapp -o yaml | grep image:
 
# Verify image exists
docker pull gcr.io/project/myapp:v1.0
 
# Fix: Correct image tag
kubectl set image deployment/myapp myapp=gcr.io/project/myapp:v1.1
B. Authentication Issues:
# Check image pull secrets
kubectl get secrets
kubectl describe secret regcred
 
# Fix: Create correct secret
kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=gcr.io \
  --docker-username=_json_key \
  --docker-password="$(cat key.json)"
 
# Add to pod spec
imagePullSecrets:
- name: regcred
C. Rate Limit (Docker Hub):
# Docker Hub rate limits: 100 pulls/6h
 
# Fix: Use authenticated pulls
kubectl create secret docker-registry dockerhub \
  --docker-username=YOUR_USERNAME \
  --docker-password=YOUR_PASSWORD

Issue 6: Persistent Volume Issues
Symptoms:
# Pod pending with PVC issue
$ kubectl get pods
NAME                 READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
myapp-abc123-xyz     0/1     Pending   0          10m
 
$ kubectl get pvc
NAME        STATUS    VOLUME   CAPACITY
data-pvc    Pending   -        -
Debugging:
# Describe PVC
kubectl describe pvc data-pvc
 
# Events:
# "no persistent volumes available"
# "storageclass not found"
# "volume size exceeded quota"
Fixes:
A. No Available PV:
# Check PVs
kubectl get pv
 
# Create PV manually or use StorageClass for dynamic provisioning
B. StorageClass Issues:
# Check StorageClass
kubectl get storageclass
 
# Fix: Create or use correct StorageClass
kubectl apply -f storageclass.yaml
 
# Update PVC
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data-pvc
spec:
  storageClassName: fast-ssd  # Specify correct class
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi

🛠️ Essential Kubectl Commands
Quick Reference
Pod Debugging:
# Get pods with details
kubectl get pods -o wide
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces
 
# Describe pod (events, conditions)
kubectl describe pod <pod-name>
 
# Logs
kubectl logs <pod-name>
kubectl logs <pod-name> --previous
kubectl logs <pod-name> -f  # Follow
kubectl logs <pod-name> -c <container-name>  # Multi-container
 
# Execute commands in pod
kubectl exec <pod-name> -- ls /app
kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -- /bin/bash
 
# Debug with ephemeral container (K8s 1.23+)
kubectl debug <pod-name> -it --image=busybox --target=<container-name>
 
# Copy files
kubectl cp <pod-name>:/app/log.txt ./log.txt
kubectl cp ./config.yaml <pod-name>:/app/config.yaml
 
# Port forward
kubectl port-forward <pod-name> 8080:80
Node Debugging:
# Node status
kubectl get nodes
kubectl top nodes
kubectl describe node <node-name>
 
# Cordon/drain node
kubectl cordon <node-name>  # Prevent scheduling
kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl uncordon <node-name>  # Allow scheduling
 
# SSH to node (GKE)
gcloud compute ssh <node-name>
Events và Logs:
# Cluster events
kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp'
kubectl get events --field-selector type=Warning
 
# Component logs
kubectl logs -n kube-system <kube-apiserver-pod>
kubectl logs -n kube-system <kube-controller-manager-pod>
Resource Usage:
# Metrics
kubectl top nodes
kubectl top pods
kubectl top pods --containers
 
# Resource requests/limits
kubectl describe node <node-name> | grep -A 5 "Allocated resources"

📊 Performance Troubleshooting
Slow Application Response
Investigation:
# 1. Check pod CPU/memory
kubectl top pod <pod-name>
 
# 2. Check application logs
kubectl logs <pod-name> | grep -i "slow\|timeout\|error"
 
# 3. Network latency
kubectl exec <pod-name> -- ping <service-name>
kubectl exec <pod-name> -- curl -w "@curl-format.txt" http://service-name
 
# curl-format.txt:
#     time_namelookup:  %{time_namelookup}\n
#        time_connect:  %{time_connect}\n
#     time_appconnect:  %{time_appconnect}\n
#    time_pretransfer:  %{time_pretransfer}\n
#       time_redirect:  %{time_redirect}\n
#  time_starttransfer:  %{time_starttransfer}\n
#                     ----------\n
#          time_total:  %{time_total}\n
Common Causes:


Database Performance:

Slow queries
Missing indexes
Connection pool exhausted



External API Calls:

Third-party API slow/down
Timeout settings too high
No circuit breaker



Resource Constraints:

CPU throttling
Memory pressure
Disk I/O bottleneck




Network Troubleshooting
Tools:
# Deploy debug pod
kubectl run debug --rm -it --image=nicolaka/netshoot -- /bin/bash
 
# Inside debug pod:
# DNS resolution
nslookup myservice
dig myservice.default.svc.cluster.local
 
# Connectivity
ping myservice
curl http://myservice:80
 
# Trace route
traceroute myservice
 
# Port scanning
nc -zv myservice 80
 
# tcpdump
tcpdump -i any port 80

📝 Incident Response Checklist
During Incident
□ Acknowledge alert
□ Assess severity
□ Start incident channel
□ Identify impacted services
□ Check recent changes
□ Gather logs và metrics
□ Form hypothesis
□ Test hypothesis
□ Implement fix
□ Monitor results
□ Verify fix
□ Communicate status

Post-Incident
□ Write post-mortem
□ Timeline of events
□ Root cause analysis
□ What went well
□ What didn't go well
□ Action items
□ Assign owners
□ Set deadlines
□ Follow up


🎯 Pro Tips
1. Use kubectl aliases:
alias k='kubectl'
alias kgp='kubectl get pods'
alias kd='kubectl describe'
alias kl='kubectl logs'
alias kx='kubectl exec -it'
2. Set context aliases:
alias kprod='kubectl config use-context production'
alias kstag='kubectl config use-context staging'
3. Watch resources:
watch kubectl get pods
kubectl get pods -w  # Watch mode
4. JSON path queries:
# Get pod IPs
kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.podIP}'
 
# Get container images
kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.containers[*].image}'

🎓 Key Takeaways
1. Systematic Approach:

Don’t panic
Follow debugging workflow
Document findings

2. Common Issues:

Pending: Resources, scheduling
CrashLoopBackOff: App errors, probes
ImagePullBackOff: Auth, image not found
High usage: Optimize or scale

3. Essential Tools:

kubectl logs, describe, exec
top, events
Port forwarding
Debug pods

4. Prevention:

Monitor proactively
Set up alerts
Regular testing
Keep runbooks updated

02---areas/k8s/11-production-deployment/.title: 11.9. Real-World Case Studies
02---areas/k8s/11-production-deployment/.content:
11.9. Real-World Case Studies

Kinh nghiệm thực tế từ production deployments


🎯 Mục Tiêu

✅ Học từ real-world scenarios
✅ Architecture decisions
✅ Challenges và solutions
✅ Lessons learned


🛒 Case Study 1: E-Commerce Platform
Background
Company: Online retailer
Scale: 10M users, 100K orders/day
Challenge: Black Friday traffic (10x normal)
Architecture
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         PRODUCTION CLUSTER              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                         │
│  Frontend (React SPA)                   │
│  ├─ Deployment: 10-50 pods (HPA)       │
│  ├─ Ingress: NGINX + cert-manager      │
│  └─ CDN: CloudFlare                    │
│                                         │
│  Backend Services (Microservices)       │
│  ├─ Order Service (10-30 pods)         │
│  ├─ Payment Service (5-20 pods)        │
│  ├─ Inventory Service (5-15 pods)      │
│  └─ Notification Service (3-10 pods)   │
│                                         │
│  Databases                              │
│  ├─ PostgreSQL (StatefulSet)           │
│  ├─ Redis (cache)                      │
│  └─ Elasticsearch (search)             │
│                                         │
│  Message Queue                          │
│  └─ RabbitMQ (StatefulSet)             │
│                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘

Key Decisions
1. Microservices Architecture
Why: Scalability, independent deployment
Challenge: Service discovery, distributed tracing
Solution: Istio service mesh

2. Autoscaling Strategy
# HPA based on custom metrics
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: order-service-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: order-service
  minReplicas: 10
  maxReplicas: 50
  metrics:
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: orders_per_second
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "100"  # 100 orders/sec per pod
3. Database Strategy
Primary: PostgreSQL (StatefulSet)
Read replicas: 5 replicas
Cache: Redis (80% hit rate)

Black Friday Preparation
Pre-event:
# 1. Pre-scale infrastructure
kubectl scale deployment frontend --replicas=30
kubectl scale deployment order-service --replicas=20
 
# 2. Warm up cache
# Run cache warming job
 
# 3. Load testing
# Simulate 10x traffic with k6
 
# 4. War room setup
# Incident channel, on-call rotation
During Event:
✓ Peak: 150K concurrent users
✓ Autoscaling worked perfectly
✓ 0 downtime
✓ P95 latency < 500ms
✓ 0 critical incidents

Lessons Learned
What Worked:
✓ HPA with custom metrics
✓ Pre-scaling before event
✓ Extensive load testing
✓ Monitoring dashboards
✓ Runbooks for common issues

What Didn’t:
✗ Database connection pool exhausted (fixed: increased pool size)
✗ Redis memory spike (fixed: added memory limits + eviction policy)
✗ Some alerts too noisy (fixed: adjusted thresholds)


🏢 Case Study 2: SaaS Platform Migration
Background
Company: B2B SaaS
Migration: Monolith → Microservices on K8s
Timeline: 6 months
Users: 50K companies, 500K end users
Migration Strategy
Phase 1: Strangler Pattern
Monolith (VM)
    ↓
API Gateway (K8s)
    ├─ Route to Monolith (default)
    └─ Route to new services (gradually)

Phase 2: Service by Service
Month 1-2: Auth Service → K8s
Month 3-4: User Service → K8s
Month 5-6: Core Business Logic → K8s

Architecture
# Multi-tenant architecture
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-acme
  labels:
    tenant: acme
    tier: premium
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: tenant-quota
  namespace: tenant-acme
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "10"
    requests.memory: 20Gi
    pods: "50"
Challenges & Solutions
Challenge 1: Data Migration
Problem: 500GB database
Solution: 
  • Dual-write (old + new DB)
  • Background migration job
  • Verification scripts
  • Gradual cutover

Challenge 2: Zero Downtime
Solution:
  • Feature flags
  • Canary deployments
  • Instant rollback capability
  • Extensive monitoring

Challenge 3: Multi-tenancy
Solution:
  • Namespace per tenant
  • Resource quotas
  • Network policies
  • Tenant-specific configs

Results
✓ Zero downtime during migration
✓ 40% cost reduction (vs VMs)
✓ 3x faster deployments
✓ 99.95% → 99.99% uptime
✓ Better resource utilization


🎮 Case Study 3: Gaming Backend
Background
Company: Mobile game
Scale: 5M DAU (Daily Active Users)
Challenge: Spiky traffic, real-time gameplay
Architecture
Global Load Balancer
        ↓
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│   Regional Clusters (3)       │
├───────────────────────────────┤
│                               │
│  Game Servers (StatefulSet)   │
│  ├─ Sticky sessions           │
│  ├─ 1000 pods                 │
│  └─ Autoscaling: 500-2000     │
│                               │
│  Matchmaking Service          │
│  ├─ Queue management          │
│  └─ Low latency required      │
│                               │
│  Leaderboard Service          │
│  ├─ Redis Cluster             │
│  └─ High read throughput      │
│                               │
└───────────────────────────────┘

Key Optimizations
1. Pod Affinity (Sticky Sessions)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: game-server
spec:
  serviceName: game-server
  replicas: 1000
  template:
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - weight: 100
            podAffinityTerm:
              labelSelector:
                matchExpressions:
                - key: app
                  operator: In
                  values:
                  - game-server
              topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
2. DaemonSet for Monitoring
# Low-overhead monitoring agent on every node
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: game-metrics
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: metrics
        image: game-metrics:v1
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 128Mi
3. Spot Instances for Non-Critical
Game Servers: On-demand (critical)
Analytics: Spot instances (70% cheaper)
Batch jobs: Spot instances

Incident: Traffic Spike
Event: Viral TikTok video → 10x traffic
Impact: Cluster autoscaler couldn’t keep up
Response:
# 1. Emergency scale
kubectl scale statefulset game-server --replicas=2000
 
# 2. Request more quota from cloud provider
 
# 3. Enable aggressive autoscaling
kubectl patch hpa game-server-hpa --patch '
spec:
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 100
        periodSeconds: 15
'
Prevention:
✓ Pre-provisioned spare capacity
✓ Faster autoscaling policies
✓ Better monitoring/alerting
✓ Runbook for traffic spikes


📊 Common Patterns
Pattern 1: Gradual Rollout
All migrations used:
• Feature flags
• Canary deployments
• Extensive monitoring
• Quick rollback capability

Pattern 2: Observability First
Before production:
• Metrics collection
• Log aggregation
• Distributed tracing
• Alerting rules
• Dashboards

Pattern 3: Cost Optimization
• Right-size resources
• Use spot instances
• Cluster autoscaling
• Namespace quotas
• Regular cost reviews


🎓 Key Lessons
Technical:
✓ Start with monitoring
✓ Automate everything
✓ Test failure scenarios
✓ Have rollback plans
✓ Use GitOps

Process:
✓ Gradual migrations
✓ Feature flags
✓ War room for big events
✓ Post-mortems
✓ Runbooks

People:
✓ Train team on K8s
✓ On-call rotation
✓ Clear ownership
✓ Documentation
✓ Knowledge sharing


💡 Recommendations
For Startups:
• Start with managed K8s (GKE/EKS)
• Use simple architecture first
• Focus on core features
• Optimize later

For Enterprises:
• Gradual migration (strangler pattern)
• Multi-cluster for isolation
• Invest in platform team
• Compliance from day 1

For High-Traffic:
• Multi-region deployment
• Aggressive autoscaling
• Extensive load testing
• Chaos engineering


⬅️ 11.8. Troubleshooting | 🏠 Mục Lục

02---areas/k8s/11-production-deployment/.title: Phần 11: Production Deployment
02---areas/k8s/11-production-deployment/.content:
📘 Phần 11: Production Deployment

Deploy K8s applications to production


🎯 Mục Tiêu
✅ Production cluster setup (GKE/EKS)
✅ CI/CD integration (GitLab CI, ArgoCD)
✅ Security hardening (RBAC, PSS, Network Policies)
✅ Monitoring & Logging stack
✅ Backup & DR strategies
✅ Cost optimization
✅ Troubleshooting production issues

📚 Production Checklist
Cluster Setup
✓ Managed K8s (GKE, EKS, AKS)
✓ Multi-zone for HA
✓ Node pools với autoscaling
✓ Network policies enabled
✓ Private cluster (if possible)
✓ Terraform for IaC
Security
✓ RBAC configured
✓ Pod Security Standards enforced
✓ Network Policies implemented
✓ Secrets encrypted at rest
✓ Image scanning (Trivy)
✓ Admission controllers (OPA)
✓ Regular security audits
Observability
✓ Metrics: Prometheus + Grafana
✓ Logs: Loki or ELK
✓ Traces: Jaeger
✓ Alerting: AlertManager
✓ Dashboards: Golden signals
✓ SLIs/SLOs defined
CI/CD
✓ GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux)
✓ Automated testing
✓ Security scanning
✓ Progressive delivery (canary)
✓ Rollback automation
✓ Image signing/verification
Backup & DR
✓ etcd backups (automated)
✓ Application data backups (Velero)
✓ Multi-region strategy
✓ RTO/RPO defined
✓ DR testing regular

🚀 Deployment Strategies
Rolling Update (Default)
strategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 1
    maxUnavailable: 0
 
# Zero downtime
# Gradual rollout
# Easy rollback
Blue-Green
Blue (current): 100% traffic
Green (new): Deploy, test
Switch: Route 100% to Green
Rollback: Switch back to Blue

Canary
v1.0: 90% traffic
v2.0: 10% traffic (canary)
Monitor metrics
Gradually increase v2.0 traffic
Full rollout or rollback based on metrics


🏗️ Infrastructure as Code
Terraform Example:
# GKE Cluster
resource "google_container_cluster" "primary" {
  name     = "production-cluster"
  location = "us-central1"
  
  # Multi-zone for HA
  node_locations = [
    "us-central1-a",
    "us-central1-b",
    "us-central1-c",
  ]
  
  # Network
  network_policy {
    enabled = true
  }
  
  # Workload Identity
  workload_identity_config {
    workload_pool = "${var.project}.svc.id.goog"
  }
}
 
# Node Pool
resource "google_container_node_pool" "primary_nodes" {
  cluster    = google_container_cluster.primary.name
  node_count = 3
  
  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 3
    max_node_count = 10
  }
  
  node_config {
    machine_type = "n1-standard-4"
    disk_size_gb = 100
    
    oauth_scopes = [
      "www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
    ]
    
    labels = {
      environment = "production"
    }
  }
}

🔒 Security Hardening
Pod Security Standards:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: production
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
Network Policy (Default Deny):
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-all
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
RBAC:
# Principle of least privilege
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: developer
  namespace: development
rules:
- apiGroups: ["", "apps"]
  resources: ["pods", "deployments", "services"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch"]
  # NO delete in production!

📊 Monitoring Stack
Prometheus + Grafana:
# Install kube-prometheus-stack
helm repo add prometheus-community prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts
helm install prometheus prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack \
  --namespace monitoring \
  --create-namespace \
  --values custom-values.yaml
 
# Includes:
# - Prometheus (metrics)
# - Grafana (dashboards)
# - AlertManager (alerts)
# - Node Exporter (node metrics)
# - kube-state-metrics (K8s metrics)
Essential Dashboards:

Cluster overview
Node metrics
Pod metrics
Deployment status
Ingress traffic
etcd health


🔄 GitOps với ArgoCD
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: webapp-production
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: github.com/company/k8s-manifests
    targetRevision: main
    path: production/webapp
  destination:
    server: kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: production
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
    syncOptions:
    - CreateNamespace=true

💰 Cost Optimization
Strategies:
1. RIGHT-SIZING
   ✓ Set appropriate resource requests/limits
   ✓ Monitor actual usage
   ✓ Adjust based on data
 
2. AUTOSCALING
   ✓ HPA for Pods
   ✓ Cluster Autoscaler for Nodes
   ✓ VPA for resource optimization
 
3. SPOT/PREEMPTIBLE INSTANCES
   ✓ Use for non-critical workloads
   ✓ Can save 60-80% costs
   ✓ Implement graceful handling
 
4. RESOURCE CLEANUP
   ✓ Delete unused PVCs
   ✓ Remove old Docker images
   ✓ Clean up failed Jobs
 
5. MONITORING
   ✓ Kubecost for cost visibility
   ✓ Track costs per namespace/team
   ✓ Set budget alerts

🐛 Production Troubleshooting
Common Issues:
# 1. Pod CrashLoopBackOff
kubectl describe pod <pod-name>
kubectl logs <pod-name> --previous
 
# 2. ImagePullBackOff
kubectl describe pod <pod-name>
# Check imagePullSecrets
 
# 3. Service not reachable
kubectl get endpoints <service-name>
# Check selector matches Pod labels
 
# 4. High resource usage
kubectl top pods
kubectl top nodes
# Check HPA status
 
# 5. Network issues
kubectl exec <pod> -- curl <service>
# Check Network Policies
 
# 6. PVC pending
kubectl describe pvc <pvc-name>
# Check StorageClass exists
 
# 7. Node NotReady
kubectl describe node <node-name>
# Check kubelet logs

🎯 Production Day-1 Checklist
Before Go-Live:
✓ Load testing completed
✓ Disaster recovery tested
✓ Monitoring/alerting configured
✓ Runbooks documented
✓ On-call rotation established
✓ Backup verified
✓ Security scan passed
✓ Cost estimates reviewed
✓ Stakeholder approval
 
After Go-Live:
✓ Monitor metrics closely
✓ Check logs for errors
✓ Verify backup running
✓ Test rollback procedure
✓ Document incidents
✓ Collect feedback
✓ Plan improvements

🎉 You’re Production Ready!
Remember:

Start small, iterate
Monitor everything
Automate toil
Document learnings
Share knowledge
Stay updated

Good luck with your production deployment! 🚀

02---areas/k8s/quick-start.content:
🚀 Quick Start Guide

Hướng dẫn nhanh để bắt đầu với tài liệu


📖 Cấu Trúc Tài Liệu
Tài liệu được chia thành 11 phần + labs thực hành, từ cơ bản đến production:
K8S/
├── README.md                      ← BẮT ĐẦU TỪ ĐÂY (Mục lục tổng)
├── 01-introduction/               ← Phần 1: Kubernetes là gì?
├── 02-architecture/               ← Phần 2: Kiến trúc K8s
├── 03-core-concepts/              ← Phần 3: Pod, Namespace, Labels
├── 04-workloads/                  ← Phần 4: Deployment, StatefulSet...
├── 05-networking/                 ← Phần 5: Service, Ingress
├── 06-configuration/              ← Phần 6: ConfigMap, Secret, Resources
├── 07-storage/                    ← Phần 7: Volume, PV, PVC

🎓 Đối Tượng Học
🟢 Beginner (Người Mới)
Bạn là: Chưa biết gì về Kubernetes
Học theo thứ tự:

Phần 1: Introduction - Hiểu K8s là gì
Phần 2: Architecture - Kiến trúc tổng quan
Phần 3: Core Concepts - Pod, Namespace, Labels
Thực hành: Cài Minikube, chạy Pod đầu tiên
Phần 4.2: Deployment - Workload quan trọng nhất
Phần 5.1: Service - Expose ứng dụng

Thời gian: 2-3 tuần

🟡 Intermediate (Trung Cấp)
Bạn là: Đã biết Docker, muốn học K8s để deploy production
Học nhanh:

Phần 1 - Skim qua (30 phút)
Phần 2 - Đọc kỹ (2 giờ)
Phần 3 - Đọc kỹ (2 giờ)
Phần 4 - Đọc hết (3 giờ)
Phần 5 - Đọc hết (3 giờ)
Phần 6-8 - Đọc và practice (1 tuần)
Phần 9: Security - RBAC, NetworkPolicy
🧪 Labs - Thực hành từng bước

Thời gian: 2-3 tuần

🔴 Advanced (Tham Khảo Nhanh)
Bạn là: Đã dùng K8s, cần reference nhanh
Jump to:

Architecture Details
Component Workflows 🆕
Deployment Strategies
Ingress Setup
Storage Best Practices
HPA Configuration
RBAC Patterns
Production Deployment


💡 Cách Sử Dụng Tài Liệu
📖 Đọc Tuần Tự
Đọc từ Phần 1 → Phần 11. Mỗi phần xây dựng trên kiến thức phần trước.
🔍 Tham Khảo Nhanh
Dùng mục lục để jump đến phần cần tìm. Mỗi file độc lập, có đủ context.
🛠️ Thực Hành Kết Hợp
Sau mỗi phần lý thuyết, mở terminal và thực hành ngay với Labs.
📝 Ghi Chú
Thêm notes riêng của bạn vào mỗi file.

🛠️ Setup Môi Trường Học
Option 1: Minikube (Recommended cho bắt đầu)
Windows:
choco install minikube
minikube start
macOS:
brew install minikube
minikube start
Linux (Fedora):
curl -LO storage.googleapis.com/minikube/releases/latest/minikube-linux-amd64
sudo install minikube-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/minikube
minikube start
Option 2: kubeadm (Production-like — xem Lab Setup Guide)
Option 3: Docker Desktop

Cài Docker Desktop
Settings → Kubernetes → Enable Kubernetes

Option 4: Online Playground

Killercoda: killercoda.com/kubernetes (free, interactive)
Play with Kubernetes: labs.play-with-k8s.com (free, 4 hours)


📚 Tài Liệu Bổ Sung
Official Docs

Kubernetes.io: kubernetes.io/docs

kubectl Cheatsheet
# Xem pods
kubectl get pods
 
# Xem chi tiết
kubectl describe pod <pod-name>
 
# Logs
kubectl logs <pod-name>
 
# Exec vào container
kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -- /bin/bash
 
# Apply YAML
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
 
# Delete
kubectl delete pod <pod-name>
kubectl explain
# Xem docs ngay trong terminal
kubectl explain pod
kubectl explain pod.spec
kubectl explain deployment.spec.strategy

🎯 Learning Goals
Sau 1 tuần:

 Hiểu K8s là gì và giải quyết vấn đề gì
 Biết kiến trúc K8s (Control Plane, Worker Node)
 Deploy được 1 ứng dụng đơn giản

Sau 1 tháng:

 Hiểu hầu hết concepts (Pod, Deployment, Service, etc.)
 Deploy được multi-tier application
 Biết troubleshoot cơ bản

Sau 3 tháng:

 Tự tin deploy production workloads
 Biết monitoring, logging, security
 Có thể thi CKA/CKAD (nếu muốn)


❓ FAQ
Q: Tôi cần biết Docker không?
A: Nên biết Docker cơ bản, nhưng không bắt buộc. Tài liệu này giải thích từ đầu.
Q: Tôi cần biết Linux không?
A: Nên biết Linux cơ bản (cd, ls, cat, ssh). Không cần expert.
Q: Mất bao lâu để học xong?
A:

Beginner: 1-2 tháng (2-3 giờ/ngày)
Intermediate: 2-3 tuần
Đọc lướt: 1 tuần

Q: Tài liệu có YAML examples không?
A: Có, đầy đủ YAML examples chạy được, kèm giải thích chi tiết. Labs sử dụng podinfo project thực tế.
Q: Tôi nên học phần nào trước?
A: Đọc tuần tự từ Phần 1 → 11 nếu là beginner. Kết hợp Labs song song.
Q: Có cần setup cluster không?
A: Không cần ngay. Phần 1-3 là lý thuyết. Từ Phần 4 nên có Minikube. Từ Lab 01 trở đi cần cluster.

📞 Support
Cần giúp đỡ?

Kubernetes Slack: slack.k8s.io
StackOverflow: [kubernetes] tag
Reddit: r/kubernetes


🚀 Bắt Đầu Ngay!
Lộ trình đề xuất:
📖 Step 1: Đọc README.md - Mục lục tổng (5 phút)
📖 Step 2: Đọc Phần 1: Introduction (1-2 giờ)
🛠️ Step 3: Setup Minikube (30 phút)
📖 Step 4: Đọc Phần 2-3 (3-4 giờ)
🧪 Step 5: Lab 01: First Pod (30 phút)
📖 Step 6: Tiếp tục Phần 4-11, kết hợp Labs (2-3 tuần)

Good luck! 🎉

“The best way to learn Kubernetes is by breaking things and fixing them.” 💪

📘 Kubernetes Learning Guide - Hướng Dẫn Học Kubernetes Từ Đầu

Tài liệu học Kubernetes có hệ thống, dễ hiểu cho người mới bắt đầu
Đặc điểm: Giải thích bằng ví dụ thực tế • Trình bày có hệ thống • Giải thích “vì sao” chứ không chỉ định nghĩa

02---areas/k8s/labs/01-first-pod/01-crea.title: Lab 01: Chạy Pod Đầu Tiên
02---areas/k8s/labs/01-first-pod/01-crea.content:
Lab 01: Chạy Pod Đầu Tiên

🕐 25 phút | 📖 Ch01 Introduction, Ch03 Pods


🎯 Mục Tiêu

Tạo Pod imperative và declarative
Generate YAML từ --dry-run=client -o yaml
Inspect Pod: describe, logs, exec
Port-forward và test endpoints


Bước 1: Tạo Pod Imperative
kubectl run podinfo --image=ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.7.1 --port=9898
 
kubectl get pods
# NAME      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
# podinfo   1/1     Running   0          30s
 
kubectl get pods -o wide
# Ghi chú: Pod IP, Node
✅ Checkpoint

 Pod Running, biết Pod IP và Node


Bước 2: Inspect Pod
# Xem toàn bộ thông tin
kubectl describe pod podinfo
# Chú ý: Containers, Conditions, Events
 
# Logs
kubectl logs podinfo
kubectl logs podinfo -f   # follow realtime (Ctrl+C thoát)
 
# Exec vào container
kubectl exec -it podinfo -- sh
  wget -qO- localhost:9898
  wget -qO- localhost:9898/healthz
  env | head -20
  exit

💡 exec -it = interactive terminal. -i stdin open, -t allocate TTY.
Trong production hạn chế exec vì security (xem Lab 26 RBAC).

✅ Checkpoint

 describe → image, port, events
 logs → podinfo listening port 9898
 exec → shell bên trong container


Bước 3: Port-Forward và Test
kubectl port-forward pod/podinfo 8080:9898 &
 
curl localhost:8080          # JSON response
curl localhost:8080/healthz  # {"status":"ok"}
curl localhost:8080/readyz   # {"status":"ok"}
curl localhost:8080/env      # environment variables
curl localhost:8080/metrics | head -5  # Prometheus format
 
kill %1 2>/dev/null

💡 Port-forward chỉ dùng dev/debug. Production dùng Service (Lab 14) hoặc Ingress (Lab 16).

✅ Checkpoint

 curl trả về JSON, /healthz OK


Bước 4: Generate YAML từ Dry-Run

🔥 CKA Tip: Không viết YAML từ đầu — generate rồi chỉnh!

kubectl delete pod podinfo
 
# Generate YAML template
kubectl run podinfo --image=ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.7.1 --port=9898 \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml > podinfo-pod.yaml
 
cat podinfo-pod.yaml

💡 YAML 4 phần bắt buộc:
apiVersion: v1        # API group + version
kind: Pod             # Resource type
metadata:             # Tên, namespace, labels
  name: podinfo
spec:                 # Desired state — PHẦN QUAN TRỌNG NHẤT
  containers: [...]

✅ Checkpoint

 Biết --dry-run=client -o yaml
 Hiểu 4 phần YAML


Bước 5: Tạo Pod Declarative
cat > podinfo-pod.yaml << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: podinfo
  labels:
    app: podinfo
    version: "6.7.1"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: podinfo
    image: ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.7.1
    ports:
    - containerPort: 9898
      name: http
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 64Mi
      limits:
        cpu: 250m
        memory: 128Mi
    env:
    - name: PODINFO_UI_MESSAGE
      value: "Hello from my first Pod!"
EOF
 
kubectl apply -f podinfo-pod.yaml
kubectl get pods --show-labels
 
# Test
kubectl port-forward pod/podinfo 8080:9898 &
curl -s localhost:8080 | grep message
# "message": "Hello from my first Pod!"
kill %1 2>/dev/null
✅ Checkpoint

 Pod chạy từ YAML, labels hiển thị
 Custom message xuất hiện


🧹 Cleanup
# GIỮ LẠI podinfo-pod.yaml cho Lab 02
kubectl delete pod podinfo

🔥 Troubleshooting

























Triệu chứngNguyên nhânFixPendingNode thiếu resourcesdescribe pod → EventsContainerCreating lâuPull image chậmChờ hoặc check networkPort-forward refusedPod chưa Runningget pods → wait

🎤 Interview Questions

Pod và Container khác nhau? → Pod = đơn vị nhỏ nhất K8s, chứa 1+ containers share network + volumes.
kubectl apply vs kubectl create? → create chỉ tạo mới (fail nếu có). apply tạo hoặc update.
requests vs limits? → requests = guaranteed (Scheduler dùng). limits = maximum (exceed memory → OOMKill).

02---areas/k8s/labs/01-first-pod/02-debu.title: Lab 02: Debug Broken Pod
02---areas/k8s/labs/01-first-pod/02-debu.content:
Lab 02: Debug Broken Pod

🕐 20 phút | 📖 Ch03 Pods | ⬅️ Lab 01


🎯 Mục Tiêu

Debug ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff
Sử dụng describe, logs, logs --previous
Nắm debug decision tree


Bước 1: ImagePullBackOff
kubectl run broken-image --image=ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:99.99.99
 
kubectl get pods
# broken-image   0/1   ImagePullBackOff   0   30s
 
kubectl describe pod broken-image | tail -15
# Events: Failed to pull image "...99.99.99": not found
 
kubectl delete pod broken-image
✅ Checkpoint

 Thấy ImagePullBackOff và root cause trong Events


Bước 2: CrashLoopBackOff
cat > crasher.yaml << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: crasher
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo 'Starting...'; exit 1"]
EOF
 
kubectl apply -f crasher.yaml
sleep 20
 
kubectl get pods
# crasher   0/1   CrashLoopBackOff   3   30s
 
kubectl logs crasher
# Starting...
 
kubectl logs crasher --previous
# Starting... (lần restart trước)
 
kubectl describe pod crasher | grep -A 3 "Last State"
# Reason: Error, Exit Code: 1
 
# CrashLoopBackOff backoff: 10s → 20s → 40s → 80s → ... → 5 phút max
 
kubectl delete pod crasher
rm -f crasher.yaml
✅ Checkpoint

 Thấy CrashLoopBackOff, dùng logs --previous
 Exit Code: 1 → command fails


Bước 3: Debug Decision Tree

💡 Khi Pod STATUS không phải Running:
Pending         → describe → thiếu resources? taint? PVC?
ImagePullBackOff → sai image/tag, private registry cần Secret
CrashLoopBackOff → logs + logs --previous → sai command/config
ContainerCreating → pulling image chậm, volume mount issue
Terminating kẹt  → kubectl delete pod X --force --grace-period=0


# Combo test: tạo Pod thiếu resources
cat > pending-pod.yaml << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: too-big
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "100"
        memory: 500Gi
EOF
 
kubectl apply -f pending-pod.yaml
sleep 5
 
kubectl get pods
# too-big   0/1   Pending   0   5s
 
kubectl describe pod too-big | tail -5
# 0/N nodes are available: insufficient cpu, insufficient memory
 
kubectl delete pod too-big
rm -f pending-pod.yaml
✅ Checkpoint

 Debug 3 failure modes: ImagePull, CrashLoop, Pending
 Nắm debug flow: STATUS → describe → Events → logs


🔥 Troubleshooting



































Exit CodeÝ nghĩaPhổ biến0Success (normal exit)Completed Jobs1App errorConfig sai, dependency missing127Command not foundSai binary path137SIGKILL (128+9)OOMKilled (memory limit)143SIGTERM (128+15)Graceful shutdown

🎤 Interview Questions

CrashLoopBackOff debug flow? → describe pod → Events → logs + logs --previous → fix root cause.
Exit code 137? → 128+9 = SIGKILL, thường do OOMKilled (memory vượt limit).
Pod Pending mãi? → describe pod → check Events: insufficient resources, taint/toleration, PVC not bound.

02---areas/k8s/labs/02-architecture/03-e.title: Lab 03: Khám Phá Control Plane
02---areas/k8s/labs/02-architecture/03-e.content:
Lab 03: Khám Phá Control Plane

🕐 25 phút | 📖 Ch02 Architecture | ⬅️ Lab 02


🎯 Mục Tiêu

Xem Control Plane và Worker Node components
Tương tác API Server qua kubectl proxy
Nhận diện Static Pods


Bước 1: Xem Cluster Components
kubectl cluster-info
kubectl get nodes -o wide
 
# Control Plane components — tất cả chạy trong kube-system
kubectl get pods -n kube-system
# Bạn sẽ thấy:
# etcd-xxx               — Database lưu trạng thái cluster
# kube-apiserver-xxx      — API Server, gateway duy nhất
# kube-scheduler-xxx      — Chọn Node cho Pod
# kube-controller-manager — Reconciliation loops
# coredns-xxx             — Cluster DNS
# kube-proxy-xxx          — Network proxy (DaemonSet)
# calico/cilium/flannel   — CNI plugin
 
# Mapping: Component → Vai trò
echo "=== Control Plane ==="
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l tier=control-plane -o custom-columns=\
NAME:.metadata.name,\
NODE:.spec.nodeName 2>/dev/null || \
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o custom-columns=\
NAME:.metadata.name,\
NODE:.spec.nodeName | head -10

💡 Deep Dive: Component Communication
User → kubectl → API Server → etcd (store)
                     ↓
                Scheduler (assign Pod → Node)
                     ↓
                kubelet (Node) → Container Runtime → Container

Mọi giao tiếp đều qua API Server. Không component nào nói chuyện trực tiếp.

✅ Checkpoint

 Nhận diện 5 core components: etcd, apiserver, scheduler, controller-manager, coredns


Bước 2: API Server Proxy
# Mở proxy tới API Server (không cần token)
kubectl proxy --port=8001 &
 
# List API resources
curl -s localhost:8001/api/v1 | head -20
 
# Xem namespaces
curl -s localhost:8001/api/v1/namespaces | python3 -m json.tool | head -20
 
# Xem Pod cụ thể qua API (tạo lại podinfo nếu cần)
kubectl run podinfo --image=ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.7.1 --port=9898 2>/dev/null
sleep 5
 
curl -s localhost:8001/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/podinfo | python3 -m json.tool | head -30
 
# Xem tất cả API groups
curl -s localhost:8001/apis | python3 -m json.tool | head -40
 
kill %1 2>/dev/null

💡 Mọi kubectl command đều translate thành REST calls tới API Server.
kubectl get pods = GET /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods

✅ Checkpoint

 kubectl proxy → REST API trả JSON
 Hiểu: kubectl = REST client tới API Server


Bước 3: Static Pods
# Static Pods = Managed bởi kubelet trực tiếp (KHÔNG qua API Server)
# Control plane components thường là Static Pods
 
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o custom-columns=\
NAME:.metadata.name,\
CONTROLLED-BY:.metadata.ownerReferences[0].kind 2>/dev/null | head -10
 
# Static Pods có tên kết thúc bằng -<node-name>
kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
 
# 💡 Static Pod manifest nằm trong /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ trên Node
# kubelet watch thư mục này → tạo/update Pods tự động
# Xóa file = xóa Pod, sửa file = update Pod
✅ Checkpoint

 Nhận diện Static Pods qua tên (-<node-name> suffix)
 Hiểu: Static Pods = kubelet managed, manifest files trên Node


🧹 Cleanup
# Giữ podinfo cho lab tiếp

🎤 Interview Questions

etcd lưu gì? → Toàn bộ cluster state: Pods, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets… Dạng key-value. Chỉ API Server giao tiếp với etcd.
Scheduler làm gì khi tạo Pod? → Filter nodes (resource đủ, taint match) → Score (spread, affinity) → Bind Pod tới Node tốt nhất.
Static Pods khác regular Pods? → Static do kubelet quản lý từ file manifest. Regular do API Server + Controllers quản lý. Static Pods không thể quản lý bằng kubectl delete (sẽ tạo lại).

02---areas/k8s/labs/02-architecture/04-s.title: Lab 04: Scheduling & Self-Healing
02---areas/k8s/labs/02-architecture/04-s.content:
Lab 04: Scheduling & Self-Healing

🕐 20 phút | 📖 Ch02 Architecture | ⬅️ Lab 03


🎯 Mục Tiêu

Watch scheduling events khi Pod được tạo
Hiểu self-healing qua Deployment
Thấy reconciliation loop hoạt động


Bước 1: Watch Scheduling Flow
# Watch events realtime
kubectl get events -w &
 
# Tạo Pod mới — watch events hiện ra
kubectl run test-sched --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
 
# Events bạn sẽ thấy (theo thứ tự):
# Scheduled  → Successfully assigned default/test-sched to worker-1
# Pulling    → Pulling image "busybox:1.36"
# Pulled     → Successfully pulled image
# Created    → Created container
# Started    → Started container
 
kill %1 2>/dev/null
kubectl delete pod test-sched

💡 Scheduling Flow:
kubectl create → API Server (store in etcd)
  → Scheduler: filter Nodes → score → bind to best Node
    → kubelet on that Node: pull image → create container → start


✅ Checkpoint

 Thấy 5 events: Scheduled → Pulling → Pulled → Created → Started


Bước 2: Tạo Deployment — Self-Healing
# Upgrade từ bare Pod sang Deployment
kubectl delete pod podinfo --ignore-not-found
 
kubectl create deployment podinfo \
  --image=ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.7.1 \
  --replicas=3 \
  --port=9898
 
# Watch Deployment + Pods
kubectl get deployment podinfo
kubectl get pods -l app=podinfo
# 3 Pods running
 
# Xem Deployment → ReplicaSet → Pods hierarchy
kubectl get rs -l app=podinfo
✅ Checkpoint

 Deployment tạo 3 Pods
 ReplicaSet tự động tạo bởi Deployment


Bước 3: Test Self-Healing
# Xóa 1 Pod — Deployment tạo ngay Pod mới!
POD=$(kubectl get pods -l app=podinfo -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
kubectl delete pod $POD
 
# Check ngay — Pod mới xuất hiện!
kubectl get pods -l app=podinfo
# Vẫn 3 Pods (1 mới thay thế)
 
# Xóa 2 Pods cùng lúc
kubectl delete pods -l app=podinfo --field-selector=status.phase=Running --wait=false
kubectl get pods -l app=podinfo -w &
sleep 10
kill %1 2>/dev/null
 
# Vẫn luôn duy trì 3 Pods!
kubectl get pods -l app=podinfo

💡 Reconciliation Loop:
Controller-Manager liên tục: desired state (3) ≠ current state (2) → tạo thêm Pod.
Đây là core principle của K8s: Declarative desired state, automatic reconciliation.

✅ Checkpoint

 Delete Pod → Deployment tạo Pod mới tự động
 Luôn duy trì desired replicas


🧹 Cleanup
# GIỮ LẠI deployment podinfo → dùng cho Lab 05

🎤 Interview Questions

Self-healing hoạt động thế nào? → Controller-Manager watch desired vs actual state. Nếu Pod die → controller tạo Pod mới để match desired replicas.
Bare Pod vs Deployment? → Bare Pod: không self-healing, không rolling update. Deployment: self-healing + rolling update + rollback. Luôn dùng Deployment.
Reconciliation loop là gì? → Controller liên tục compare desired state (spec) vs current state (status). Nếu khác → take action để converge.

02---areas/k8s/labs/02-architecture/05-n.title: Lab 05: Node Maintenance
02---areas/k8s/labs/02-architecture/05-n.content:
Lab 05: Node Maintenance

🕐 20 phút | 📖 Ch02 Architecture | ⬅️ Lab 04


🎯 Mục Tiêu

Xem Node capacity vs allocatable
Cordon Node (ngừng schedule)
Drain Node (di chuyển Pods)
Uncordon Node


Bước 1: Node Resources
kubectl get nodes -o wide
 
# Capacity vs Allocatable
kubectl describe node $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') | grep -A 8 "Capacity\|Allocatable"
# Capacity   = tổng resources vật lý
# Allocatable = resources khả dụng cho Pods (trừ system reserved)
 
# Resource usage hiện tại
kubectl top nodes     # CPU/Memory usage per Node
kubectl top pods      # CPU/Memory usage per Pod
✅ Checkpoint

 Biết Capacity vs Allocatable
 kubectl top hiển thị usage


Bước 2: Cordon & Drain
# Xem Pods phân bố trên Nodes
kubectl get pods -l app=podinfo -o wide
 
# Cordon = đánh dấu Node "SchedulingDisabled"
WORKER=$(kubectl get nodes --selector='!node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane' -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
echo "Cordon: $WORKER"
 
kubectl cordon $WORKER
kubectl get nodes
# worker-1   Ready,SchedulingDisabled
 
# Tạo Pod mới → sẽ KHÔNG schedule lên Node đã cordon
kubectl run cordon-test --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl get pod cordon-test -o wide
# Node: worker-2 (KHÔNG phải worker-1)
kubectl delete pod cordon-test
 
# Uncordon
kubectl uncordon $WORKER
kubectl get nodes
# worker-1   Ready
✅ Checkpoint

 Cordon → SchedulingDisabled
 Pods mới không schedule lên cordoned Node


Bước 3: Drain — Di Chuyển Pods
# Drain = cordon + evict tất cả Pods trên Node
kubectl get pods -l app=podinfo -o wide
 
kubectl drain $WORKER --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
 
# Pods trên $WORKER sẽ bị evict → Deployment tạo Pods mới trên Node khác
kubectl get pods -l app=podinfo -o wide
# Tất cả Pods chạy trên Nodes còn lại
 
# Uncordon — cho phép schedule trở lại
kubectl uncordon $WORKER
 
# 💡 Drain dùng khi:
# - Upgrade kernel/OS trên Node
# - Replace hardware
# - Scale down cluster

💡 Cordon vs Drain:

























CordonDrainExisting PodsGiữ nguyênEvict raNew PodsKhông scheduleKhông scheduleUse caseTạm dừng scheduleMaintenance (reboot)

✅ Checkpoint

 Drain evict Pods khỏi Node
 Deployment tạo Pods mới trên Node khác


🧹 Cleanup
# Giữ deployment podinfo cho labs tiếp

🎤 Interview Questions

Cordon vs Drain? → Cordon chỉ chặn schedule mới. Drain = cordon + evict existing Pods.
Drain có downtime không? → Nếu có PDB (Lab 25) và đủ replicas → không. PDB bảo vệ min available.
--ignore-daemonsets tại sao cần? → DaemonSet Pods chạy trên mọi Node, không thể evict. Flag này skip chúng.
